where if Aeschylus wrote ἐπικρανεῖ [he accomplishes], which is uncertain, he lengthened the penultimate syllable, which very rarely happens in this class of verbs. The present ἐπικραίνει [he accomplishes] or, as Bamberger conjectured, ἀντεπικραίνει [he accomplishes in return] is hardly probable after the future ἀποτίσει [he will pay back].
And truly the revered Erinys of father Oedipus accomplished true things.
Turning aside, she accomplished the bitter end of the marriage.
But now if he pays back the blood of those before, and dying for the dead he accomplishes the requital of other deaths.
To accomplish unjustly a graceless favor in return for great deeds.
To accomplish the gods' exemption from my prayers.
Or do you hear, bulwark of the city, what things he accomplishes (thus from the copy for ἐπικρανεῖ [he accomplishes])?
Most glorious of griefs, he accomplished.
And on thrones with single scepter you accomplish every debt.
And Zeus accomplished (I corrected to ἐπικράναι [to accomplish]) the end.
And may Zeus with fruit-bringing offering accomplish the earth in due season.
I rejoice that these things are being accomplished favorably for my land.
And by name the fated age was being accomplished.
